levers.domain_notes: Sourcing: scholarly APIs first for IR/classification/eval literature (OpenAlex, CORE); official current docs (verified via Context7/fetch, as of September 2026) for every selected library; Kaggle dataset docs and repo issues for conversation-reconstruction facts. Evidence norms: measured workspace benchmarks outrank vendor claims; GitHub maintenance/issues outrank stars. Recency window: last 1-2 years for models, frameworks, and eval tooling; older foundations acceptable for BM25/classification statistics.

rationale.inference_depth: core evidence comes from workspace inspection and measured experiments plus documented methods; revisit at loci analysis if corpus shows answers living in gray literature or closed vendor docs

scope_conditions: audit target is the existing Hiver workspace at C:\Hiver (previous AI-agent session output); do not assume correctness or preserve bad design
one brand only, selected by evidence for submission quality (not raw row count)
Banking77 for intent work ONLY; never to inflate headline results
evaluators run a subsample only; optimize for fast reproducible subsample (<15 min), not full 3M-row processing
minimum-complexity principle: simplest architecture achieving required quality; every component must earn its place by measurement
no fabricated numbers: unmeasured quantities reported as NOT MEASURED or ESTIMATED
current documentation verified as of September 14, 2026 for every selected technology
frontend work only after core AI/eval quality is established
sub_questions: What would a reviewer criticize about the CURRENT Hiver implementation, layer by layer, and what measured evidence supports each criticism?
Which single brand maximizes submission quality (response coverage, thread depth, intent diversity, resolution availability, golden-set sufficiency, escalation opportunities) and why?
What small intent taxonomy is actually grounded in the selected brand's data, and how was it derived (clustering/embeddings/topic discovery + manual inspection)?
What data split (temporal vs random, conversation-aware) prevents train/test thread overlap, near-duplicate, response, and retrieval-contamination leakage?
What defensible sampling + labelling methodology yields the 150-250 golden set (stratification, difficulty, temporal holdout, hard negatives)?
Which trivial baseline (majority/always-escalate/fixed-response) and which simple baseline (TF-IDF/BM25/embedding-NN/simple classifier/direct LLM) make honest comparisons, and what do they score?
Which retrieval design (BM25 vs embeddings vs hybrid+rerank vs thread-aware, conversation-level indexing) retrieves problems WITH useful resolutions, and how is retrieval evaluated independently?
Which per-component model choice (across OpenAI/Anthropic/Google/open-weight/local/routers) is justified by measurement rather than brand strength?
Is any agent/workflow framework necessary, or does measured evidence favor removing it?
What calibrated escalation policy (signals, thresholds, coverage-vs-quality curve) automates only what is safe to automate?

What LLM-judge rubric dimensions (correctness, relevance, grounding, usefulness, brand fit, hallucination, tone, escalation) are appropriate, and how much does the judge agree with humans (correlation/agreement + disagreement analysis)?
What are the top 5 real failure modes with real examples, hypotheses, root causes, and mitigation status?
What is misleading about the headline number — in what concrete ways could it exaggerate performance?
What was deliberately NOT built, and what would one additional week buy?

Which technology wins each capability (data/storage/retrieval/ML/eval/observability/deploy/security/testing) and why were alternatives rejected (cost/latency/reliability/scalability/maintenance/risk)?
Why should a reasonable reviewer trust this agent over a simple LLM wrapper?
